title: Two-week Intent Map and Impact Journal — Anita Bose
content:
Purpose
- Quick personal tracker for the next two weeks (sprint-ish) focusing on measurable output + learning. Not official OKR yet — a working draft for decisions and rituals.

Top objective (candidate):
- Increase predictable low-latency tail for hosted text-gen endpoints so product features relying on streaming have <150ms p50 and p99 < 600ms for 512 tokens (experimental target).

Proposed key results (draft):
1) Reduce mean inference latency for 512-token baseline by 12% (measured on staging profile 'redwood/fast-512')
2) Identify 3 concrete batching/caching policies that reduce cost-per-1000-tokens by >=8% without degrading p50 latency by >5%
3) Run 2 A/B evals on live traffic for fallback policy heuristics and verify no >1% drop in success rate for streaming connections

Weekly check-in template (fill 2x/week)
- Date: ___
- Metric snapshot (p50/p95/p99 for 128/512 tokens): p50: __ / p95: __ / p99: __
- Small wins: (1-3 bullet lines)
- Blockers: (what's stuck, who to ping)
- Hypothesis to test next: (short)
- Next actions (owner + ETA)

Week A (notes) — 2026-02-25 -> 2026-03-03
- Quick metrics: staging p50 160ms (512), p99 700ms — trending a touch worse after kernel bump.
- Win: confirmed that changing continuous-batch size cap from 32->24 lowers p99 by ~8% in synthetic bench.
- Blocker: infra/canary infra flaky — need SRE to stabilize the multitenant node for repeated runs. Pinged Noor on SRE.
- Hypothesis: smaller per-model reserve improves tail by reducing queue churn under medium burst loads. Test: synthetic spike test with per-model-reserve = [0.5, 0.8, 1.0].
- Actions: make bench-suite variation (Anita) by Wed; coordinate SRE canary (Ravi) by Thu.

Week B (notes) — 2026-03-04 -> 2026-03-10
- Metrics: after reserve=0.8 test, p50 stable, p99 improved ~6% but cost CPU on tiny hosts increased.
- Win: drafted 3 policy knobs for Optimize UI: dynamic-reserve, batch-cap, aggressive-prefix-cache.
- Retro note: I spend too much time chasing single test regressions; need to formalize acceptance criteria for bench runs so I can hand off.
- Actions: capture acceptance checklist for bench runs + add to confluence (Anita) by Fri; ask Lina to review policy UI text by next Tue.

Retrospective — what worked / what didn't
- Worked: short focused experiments gave actionable deltas (batch cap adjustments had clear p99 impact).
- Didn't: long-running bench runs without deterministic seeds wasted time. Need reproducibility.
- Personal: my calendar is heavy — prioritize 3 deep blocks per day (mornings) to ship the bench-suite changes.

Quick experiments backlog (prioritized)
- E1: continuous-batch cap sweep (24/32/40) with steady-state + spike; metric: p99 + cost delta. (On deck)
- E2: per-model reserve fraction experiments across heterogenous workload mix; metric: tail stability and cold-start failures. (Running)
- E3: prefix cache retention policy (size vs hit-rate) — cheap sim using 10M token trace. (Planned)
- E4: fallback-to-small-variant timings (how often + how fast) — tie to error budget. (Idea)

Acceptance criteria (for a bench variation to be actionable)
- 3 independent runs with identical seed/config, relative delta consistent within 3% for p50 and 8% for p99.
- Cost calculation: report token-minute cost normalized to baseline commit abc123.
- Test notes: include exact kernel commit, model variant id, and trace id.

Personal TODOs (next 2 weeks)
- Finalize bench-suite config flags and document in PR. (Anita — 2026-03-05)
- Create confluence page for 'tail-improvement-playbook' with example policy rollouts + rollback steps. (Anita/Lina — 2026-03-09)
- Run live traffic A/B for fallback heuristic with 1% sample (Ravi to coordinate infra). (Ravi — 2026-03-11)
- Draft short status slide for weekly sync: 3 bullets + 1 ask. (Anita — recurring Fridays)

Quick decision log (notes to self)
- 2026-03-01: decided to prioritize p99 over raw cost for next sprint because product impact on streaming UX is higher.
- 2026-03-08: revert kernel bump on canary if p99 regresses beyond 10% vs baseline.

Open questions / risks
- Can we synthesize a realistic mixed traffic trace that approximates real routing splits (dedicated vs hosted)? If not, bench runs might not generalize.
- Is there an inexpensive way to emulate connection churn for streaming clients?

Meeting prompts (for sync with SRE / infra)
- Can you reproduce p99 spike on the canary with the same kernel commit? (bring trace id)
- What's the expected stability SL for the canary pool? How many reruns before we call flaky?
- If we adopt dynamic-reserve policy, what operational metrics should we alert on?

Notes to self (short)
- When stuck, write the hypothesis + minimal test plan in this doc before coding. Forces clarity.
- Limit bench variations to 2 params per run to keep signal.

Archive snapshot (bench ids)
- bench/run-20260302-a1 (continuous-batch sweep)
- bench/run-20260306-b2 (per-model-reserve 0.8)

End of scratchpad.

(If this grows: migrate final playbook to shared_drives/product/hosted-api/tail-improvement-playbook.md)
